spark.scene: True-color view of the main Hawaiian Islands from Kauai in the northwest to Hawaii in the southeast. Dark ocean with scattered white cumulus, cirrus and frontal clouds to the west, north and south, with extensive white cloud over the eastern half of the large island and partly cloudy smaller islands.

plumes.label: thin pale gray streak southwest of the large island
plumes.visual_description: very faint pale gray-blue veil extending west-southwest from the southern part of the large island over the dark ocean, distinct from brighter white cumulus clouds

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

per_plume.source_hint: faint WSW veil off south Hawaii Island, vent or fire undetermined
evidence: USGS HVO at image time reports Kilauea not erupting/paused (ADVISORY/YELLOW) and Mauna Loa not erupting (NORMAL/GREEN), so sustained vog emission is not expected. [E1]
FIRMS shows no fire clusters in the plume box, only Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal pixels, giving no support for wildfire_smoke. [E6]
Mask is almost entirely oceanic (land_frac 0.003) with no island swallowed, so the streak is a real offshore veil, not a land-mask artifact, distinct from bright white cumulus. [E4]

Motion vs wind: measured drift toward 221 deg at 6.3 km/h versus wind toward ~249 deg WSW at source (from 069 deg) and toward ~183 deg at centroid (from 003 deg); differences ~28-38 deg are within ~45 deg but tracking fit is poor (R2 0.27), so transport to WSW is broadly consistent yet weak. [E7, E2, E5]

Source attribution is ambiguous: tracked source end is 20.0 km from Kilauea and 19.3 km from Mauna Loa (indistinguishable), while geometric upwind end using northerly wind is 106.5 km from Kilauea and 72.2 km from Mauna Loa. [E5, E8]

evidence_cited.text: USGS HVO at image time reports Kilauea not erupting/paused (ADVISORY/YELLOW) and Mauna Loa not erupting (NORMAL/GREEN), so sustained vog emission is not expected.
FIRMS shows no fire clusters in the plume box, only Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal pixels, giving no support for wildfire_smoke.
Mask is almost entirely oceanic (land_frac 0.003) with no island swallowed, so the streak is a real offshore veil, not a land-mask artifact, distinct from bright white cumulus.

Motion vs wind: measured drift toward 221 deg at 6.3 km/h versus wind toward ~249 deg WSW at source (from 069 deg) and toward ~183 deg at centroid (from 003 deg); differences ~28-38 deg are within ~45 deg but tracking fit is poor (R2 0.27), so transport to WSW is broadly consistent yet weak.

Source attribution is ambiguous: tracked source end is 20.0 km from Kilauea and 19.3 km from Mauna Loa (indistinguishable), while geometric upwind end using northerly wind is 106.5 km from Kilauea and 72.2 km from Mauna Loa.

classify.caveats: Feature is very faint; both volcanoes officially not erupting so active vog not expected, yet residual haze cannot be excluded. Tracking fit is poor (R2 0.27) and 10-m wind is only a proxy for plume-level transport. No fires detected but FIRMS is a single-date snapshot.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting. The summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Reinflation has been minimal since the end of lava fountaining episode 54; more data are needed to model the forecast window for the next episode.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
